name: Lacrosse Scoreboard
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Live, recent, and upcoming NCAA men's and women's lacrosse games with real-time scores and schedules

api_requirements.name: ESPN API
api_requirements.description: ESPN public API for NCAA lacrosse scores and schedules
api_requirements.rate_limit: No official rate limit, but please use responsibly

versions.notes: Validation-sweep fixes; see the PR for the specific defect.

versions.changelog: Render text 1-bit (no anti-aliasing) so glyphs stay crisp on the LED grid

versions.notes: Render the font the settings page advertises. Each text element's schema names a default font, but several elements never passed it to the loader, so the loader used its own fallback instead: the status text -- and on hockey the detail and odds text too -- advertised the 4x6 font while actually drawing in PressStart2P. Choosing the font the picker already showed as active therefore changed the display, which looked like the picker was broken. Each element now renders what its schema declares. This affects panels 128 pixels wide and narrower, on upcoming screens only; wider panels draw that header in the time font and are unchanged. It also fixes a knock-on problem: "Next Game" needed 72px in the wrong font and had to shorten to "Next" on a 64px panel, where it now fits whole at 41px.
versions.changelog: Retry a team logo whose previous download failed, instead of showing a grey box forever. A failed download is cached by the core as a placeholder wearing the real logo's filename; the logo loader scans filename variations, found that stub, and so never called the downloader again. The loader now skips a placeholder that is stale enough to be worth retrying and lets the download run, which also picks up stubs already on disk. The retry is rate-limited by the core (6h), so this does not trade a permanent grey box for a request every frame. Needs a core carrying src.logo_downloader.is_placeholder_logo; against an older core the check is skipped and behaviour is unchanged. Ported byte-identically across every sports lineage.
changes: Rewrote the README as a complete settings reference covering all 170 settings, with rendered examples of every display mode and both leagues.

versions.notes: Fix every grid-snapped font rendering a pixel narrow. The shared code reads this plugin's config_schema.json to tell a default font size from one the user chose; a default gets snapped to the font's pixel grid, a choice is left alone. It located the schema by inspecting loaded modules, which fails under the real plugin loader -- the loader renames a plugin's modules and removes their original names, so nothing was left to inspect. The lookup returned nothing, every size then looked user-chosen, and the snap was skipped: 4x6-font.ttf drew at 6 instead of 7, which is 3-pixel-wide glyphs instead of 4. On a 256x64 panel the betting odds, team records and the date row were hard to read. The plugin now tells the shared code where it lives instead of leaving it to guess.

versions.notes: The sports.py logic every scoreboard shares moves to the core. Forty-five method bodies here were byte-identical to the same forty-five in every other scoreboard -- the selection and rotation engine, the font, colour and date subsystem, and the switch-mode upcoming card -- so they now come from src.common.sports_shared and this plugin inherits them. 1040 lines removed here. A fix to any of that now reaches every scoreboard at once instead of needing eight identical edits. Three deliberately stayed behind: _get_timezone, because it binds a per-plugin timezone module whose contents differ, and the two abstract stubs that define what makes this sport its own. Nothing drawn changes -- the bodies moved rather than being rewritten, and all 176 safety-harness renders across the eight plugins are byte-identical to before. The floor rises to 3.3.0, the release that first ships the shared module.

versions.notes: Make the odds text settings visible in the web UI. The odds_text block shipped in the schema but not in x-propertyOrder, and the config form iterates that list and nothing else -- so the font, size and colour controls existed and could not be reached. Nothing about what is drawn changes; the settings simply become editable.
versions.changelog: The card helpers move to the core. Twenty methods in this plugin's game_renderer.py were byte-identical to the same twenty in every other scoreboard: the colour pickers, the scroll_card settings lookup, the date and time formatting, the favourite-team rules and the font-size grid snapping. They now live in src.common.sports_card and this plugin delegates to them, so a fix to any of that reaches every scoreboard at once instead of needing eight identical edits, and a new scoreboard gets them by importing one module. 245 lines removed here. Nothing about what is drawn changes: the bodies were moved rather than rewritten, and all 176 safety-harness renders across the eight plugins are byte-identical to before. The floor rises to 3.3.0, the release that first ships the helper.

versions.notes: Odds get their own font, size and colour. The betting line and over/under borrowed the detail_text settings, so making them bigger on a large panel also enlarged the team records and the date row, and their green was hard-coded in the drawing call where no setting could reach it. A new customization.odds_text block controls the odds alone, in both the full-screen scorebug and the scroll/Vegas card. Nothing changes unless you set it: the defaults are exactly what was rendered before -- the same 4x6 font at the same size, and the same green -- and a config saved before this setting existed falls back to detail_text, so all 176 safety-harness renders are byte-identical to the previous version. Sizes still snap to the font's pixel grid to stay crisp, so 4x6-font.ttf gives 7, 14 or 21 and press_start gives 8 or 16.

versions.notes: The bundled scroll fallback is gone, and the plugin now requires LEDMatrix 3.2.0. scroll_display.py carried a guarded import of the core's src.common.sports_scroll with a frozen pre-adoption copy, scroll_display_legacy.py, behind it, so it kept working on a core that predated the module (B5). The copy is deleted and the import is now plain -- keeping the try/except with nothing behind it would only mislabel the failure, naming the missing scroll_display_legacy instead of the core module actually absent, which is the single log line a user gets before the scoreboard stops appearing. The floor rises to 3.2.0, the release that ships the module, and the store refuses to install or update this version onto anything older. Nothing about what is drawn changes: the frozen copy was compared method by method against the core before deleting it and carried no orchestration logic the core lacks, and every safety-harness render is unchanged.

versions.notes: The other slots now fill with games worth watching, and the settings that govern them take effect. football-scoreboard has had this since 2.29.0; these eight lineages had the settings in their schema and nothing reading them, so a board could ask for ranked games only and still get the next N kickoffs. The non-favourite pool is now ordered by the matchup rather than the clock, filtered by quality and division, and re-cut on the display path every other_rotation_interval_seconds so a long pool rotates instead of showing its first N forever. Favourites keep their slots through every cut, one game per team, and the filters fail open as a set: if a filter matches nothing the mode shows the unfiltered list rather than going blank. Also retires the 'broadcast' tier of other_games_min_quality, matching football-scoreboard 3.0.0. Measured there against a real Week 1 and Week 2 college slate it passed 174 of 175 games -- ESPN publishes a broadcaster for nearly everything now, ESPN+ included -- so it read as a quality bar and behaved as 'any'. A board still holding the old value now migrates to 'ranked' with a warning rather than silently getting no filtering, and the option is gone from the settings UI.

versions.notes: Recent games now get their odds. SportsUpcoming fetches odds for the games that survive selection and SportsLive fetches them per included game -- the Recent screen never fetched them at all, so its 'odds if available' renderer never had anything attached and every final rendered bare. update() now fetches odds for the selected finals, exactly as Upcoming does; ESPN keeps a completed game's closing line on the same endpoint, so a final is as answerable as an upcoming game. Same fix as football-scoreboard 2.29.3, which only surfaced there because football's display-path rotation attached odds to rotated-in finals by accident -- this plugin has no such rotation, so its finals were bare in every configuration.

versions.notes: The rank badge now chooses the ranking block rather than taking ESPN's first. That endpoint returns several blocks and the first is not promised to be a poll: men's and women's college hockey front NCAA tournament SEEDINGS, and this league's poll sits beside seedings of its own, so the badge was one reordering away from showing a bracket seed where a viewer expects a poll position. ESPN's order is kept among genuine polls; seedings and lower divisions are stepped over. Ported from the same fix in hockey-scoreboard, which shares this code. The never-populated upcoming_games/recent_games attributes are removed: nothing filled them and nothing read them, and their presence is what made a duration calculation reading them look correct. No behaviour change here. The shared favourite-check advisory is brought back in step with football-scoreboard 2.29.4, which fixed it there without porting: the "nothing on until" line pooled event dates with the league calendar's week and phase boundaries and took the earliest, and those boundaries open days before the first game, so a boundary was reported as a game date. Events now win; the calendar only speaks for a payload with no events at all. The copies are byte-identical again, which hockey-scoreboard's test_favorite_check.py enforces across all seven.

versions.notes: Recent games come back when favourite teams are set. SportsRecent.update() calls self._favorites_first(...), but that helper -- and _other_games_window and _is_favorite_game with it -- was defined on SportsUpcoming, a sibling class rather than an ancestor, so the call raised AttributeError. update() catches it, logs "Error updating recent games" and carries on with an empty list, so the recent screen simply showed nothing. It only bites when favourite teams are configured without show_favorite_teams_only, which is the ordinary way to use the setting. football-scoreboard already had all three helpers on SportsCore and was unaffected; this brings the rest into line with it. No other behaviour changes: every safety-harness render for the seven plugins whose fixtures set no favourites is byte-identical.

versions.notes: The score is now the headline it was always meant to be. It was the only element on the card not sized from the panel, and it was not even bigger than its neighbours: PressStart2P renders crisply on an 8px grid, so the 10px default snapped to 8 -- the same 8 the clock above it and the game date below it are drawn at. It is now sized from display_height, snapped to its face's pixel grid and capped at twice its design size, with the clock/date face held a grid step below it. Score and date positions scale with their faces so a grown one is not clipped off the card. Where the grown score would swamp the panel the layout now reaches for a narrower FACE rather than crowding out the logos, which is what football-scoreboard has always done and the single reason its logos read larger than every other scoreboard's at the same size. Measured on a 128x64 board: 4x6-font at 14px reserves 28px and leaves 52x52 logos, where PressStart2P at 16px reserved 60px and left 36x36 -- two small badges adrift in a mostly black panel. The two faces are nothing like the same shape: PressStart2P is square, 4x6-font is nearly as tall and about half as wide, so the score keeps the dimension that carries legibility and gives back the one the logos need. Logos are sized against the space the score actually needs, and only where the score grew -- a panel whose score did not move keeps exactly the logos it had. The upcoming screen is untouched at every size: it draws no score, so none of this applies to it -- its date and time keep the face and size they always had. Measured on the live and recent screens: 64x32, 128x32 and 256x32 render byte-identically to the previous release, and every taller panel gains a larger score with logos the score is no longer drawn across.

versions.notes: The text colour pickers in Customization now actually colour the text. score_text, period_text, team_name, status_text, detail_text and rank_text have each offered a colour in the web UI for as long as they have had a font, and setting one changed only which font was loaded -- every string was drawn white. The colour now follows the face it belongs to, on the full-screen scoreboard and on the scroll and Vegas cards alike. Every default is white, so a display nobody has recoloured looks exactly as it did.

Every default is white, so a display nobody has recoloured looks exactly as it did.

versions.notes: Fix a crash when the date format is set to "weekday". game_renderer.py used datetime, timezone and ZoneInfo without importing any of them, so choosing that option -- one of the documented values of scroll_card.date_format -- raised NameError. Neither helper's except clause catches NameError (_weekday_for catches ValueError/TypeError, _card_tzinfo catches KeyError/ValueError/TypeError/OSError), so it propagated out of the render rather than falling back to the plain date. The imports now match hockey-scoreboard, the one copy that always had them and rendered the option correctly. Nothing else changes: the default "abbrev" format, which is what the render harness and the golden images exercise, was never affected, which is how this went unnoticed.

The matchup separator and the date and time formats now reach the full-screen scoreboard, not just the scroll and Vegas cards. A new "Middle of a Full-Screen Upcoming Scoreboard" setting (switch_upcoming_center) picks what sits between the two logos before a game starts: the stacked date and time as before, the VS / @ / at separator, nothing, or whatever the scroll and Vegas cards are set to. It defaults to the stacked date and time, so the scoreboard looks exactly as it did until you change it.

versions.notes: Favorite teams now appear in upcoming and recent even when 'show favorite teams only' is off. New other_upcoming_games_to_show / other_recent_games_to_show control how many other games fill the rest, and other_rotation_interval_seconds advances that slice over time so the board works through the schedule instead of repeating the same handful.

versions.notes: Request odds only for the games that will be shown. The upcoming-games loop fetched odds for every game it collected and the caller then kept upcoming_games_to_show of them (10 by default). The loop's own comment claimed odds were fetched only for games that would be displayed, but the filter it referred to applies only when show_favorite_teams_only is set AND favourite teams are configured, and neither is the default -- so in the usual case nothing narrowed it. A live rig running college football logged 946 upcoming games in one cycle and displayed 1 of them, having made 946 separate ESPN odds requests to do it, from a Pi that is also driving the panel. The odds cache only absorbs repeats of the same event, so a wide schedule never benefited from it. Nothing about what reaches the screen changes.
versions.changelog: Corrects a log line that claimed no favourite teams were configured when they were: the schedule view is used whenever show_favorite_teams_only is off, not only when favourites are absent. It now names the teams and the setting to change.

versions.changelog: A game_card_width equal to the schema default is now treated as unchosen, so the computed card width applies. Without this the card stayed pinned at 128px on any config saved through the web UI, which left the logos SMALLER than before, not merely unchanged.

versions.notes: Request odds only for the games that will be shown. The upcoming-games loop fetched odds for every game it collected and the caller then kept upcoming_games_to_show of them (10 by default). The loop's own comment claimed odds were fetched only for games that would be displayed, but the filter it referred to applies only when show_favorite_teams_only is set AND favourite teams are configured, and neither is the default -- so in the usual case nothing narrowed it. A live rig running college football logged 946 upcoming games in one cycle and displayed 1 of them, having made 946 separate ESPN odds requests to do it, from a Pi that is also driving the panel. The odds cache only absorbs repeats of the same event, so a wide schedule never benefited from it. Nothing about what reaches the screen changes.
versions.changelog: Pixel fonts now render on their grids instead of anti-aliased: PressStart2P snaps to multiples of 8 and 4x6-font to multiples of 7, on both the scroll/Vegas cards and the regular display. A font size that merely echoes the schema default is treated as unchosen and snapped; a size you actually chose is left alone.

Make the schedule fetch window configurable. How far back and forward games are fetched was hard-coded at 14 days back and 7 forward. Days is the wrong unit for a league that plays weekly -- a whole matchweek can fall just past a short horizon and never reach the board -- so both are now advanced settings, bounded 1-60 days, with a stray or non-numeric value falling back to the default rather than raising. Defaults keep today's behaviour.
versions.changes: Back off the live-game poll while a league has nothing on, and let both the idle interval and its ceiling be configured. Saves API calls out of season and between games without delaying an in-progress game, which still resets the interval on the first fetch that finds one.

The authoritative fetch now uses the configured window too, the Recent cutoff follows it instead of a fixed 21 days, and the fields render in the web UI for every plugin.

Load the bundled fonts without depending on the process working directory. Every font this scoreboard draws with ships in the LEDMatrix core and was named relative to the cwd, which resolves only under the packaged systemd unit, whose WorkingDirectory is the install root. Anywhere else -- the plugin safety harness, a manual run from a home directory, a unit file written without WorkingDirectory -- the load raised, the caller's fallback caught it, and the scoreboard rendered in PIL's default face at the wrong metrics instead of the pixel font its layout was built around. Every direct load now goes through a resolver that tries the path as given, then the core install root, then returns the original so existing fallbacks are untouched; a configured absolute path still passes through unchanged.

Honour the configured live-game dwell instead of the data refresh rate. The rotation lived in update(), which runs on live_update_interval -- 30s by default -- so a game could only be advanced at that cadence and every configured duration was quantised to it. Measured on a live rig with four NFL games: live_game_duration=45 and non_favorite_live_game_duration=10 both produced a flat 30s rotation, and only changing live_update_interval changed anything. It is driven from display() now, so a dwell shorter than the refresh interval is reachable and a longer one is not cut short.

Match favorites against this plugin's real live-data shape. The first cut looked for an attribute holding live_games beside favorite_teams, which is true of five scoreboards and quietly false for four: cricket keeps live_matches, nrl and afl hold their managers in a dict rather than as attributes, and ufc has favorite_fighters and fighter names. Those four reported every live game as non-favorite. A celebrating game is searched too, since the live manager snapshots it out of live_games while the celebration is on screen.

Ask for more turns in the Vegas ticker while a game is live, and more again when a favorite team is playing. Only takes effect with the core's display.vegas_scroll.live_in_ticker set, which keeps the marquee running instead of handing the display to a full-screen scoreboard. The core grants a live plugin live_weight on its own; this reports the favorite case, which the core cannot see -- it knows a game is live but not whose.

Fix blurry score digits on the LED matrix: the outline-drawing helper used PIL's default anti-aliased text rendering, which blends pixel-font (PressStart2P) glyph edges into dim partial-lit pixels on a 1:1 matrix, muddying numbers (a "6" could read as a "G"). Text now draws in 1-bit font mode so every glyph -- scores, clocks, team names, status text -- renders crisp with no anti-aliasing.

Stop an out-of-season or empty mode holding a blank panel for its full display duration. This plugin's bundled sports.py was a stale fork of the core's and its three display() methods had lost their return values (the base was annotated -> None). The manager's dispatcher treats a non-boolean as success, so every mode reported content whether or not it had any, and the display controller -- which skips a mode whose display() returns False -- never skipped it. The no-games branch clears the display, so the result was a blank screen held for the whole duration. Found alongside the same fault in hockey-scoreboard, where it was reported against NHL recent and live. The methods now return True when a game was drawn and False when there was nothing to show, matching the core and the six other sports plugins.

Scroll and Vegas cards: never show 0-0 before a game starts, add a centre gap so the score or VS is not drawn on top of the team logos, and write upcoming dates as "Sep 19". A new scroll_card config block sets what fills the middle of an upcoming card (VS, or the date and time stacked), the date format (abbrev/numeric) and the centre gap in pixels. gap_between_games is now honoured in Vegas mode, which stitches its own items and previously ignored it, and its code default moves from 24 to 48 to match the config schema. The date is positioned from its measured height rather than a fixed offset, which stops "Sep 19" running past the bottom of the card in the plugins whose detail font is 10px. These settings only affect the cards built for scroll and Vegas modes; the full-screen scoreboard is drawn by a separate code path and is unchanged. Adds a fuller set of scroll_card settings: vs_text (VS, @, at, ...), date_format now covering abbrev/numeric/day_first/numeric_day_first/weekday, time_format 12h or 24h, show_date, show_time, swap_date_time, upcoming_center gains a 'none' option, and center_gap_ratio/min/max for the automatic gap. Each customization text element gains text_color, and the customization.layout X/Y offsets are now honoured by the scroll/Vegas card -- the schema advertised them but only the full-screen scoreboard read them before. The away team is drawn on the left and the home team on the right, so "at" and "@" read correctly as "away at home".

Add customization.favorite_result_colors: an optional setting that colors a recent game's final score green when your favorite team won and red when it lost. Aimed at scroll and Vegas modes, where the same matchup can go past several times and the logos alone do not say who won. Off by default; games without exactly one favorite team keep the normal score color.

Fix ESPN 403s. Around 2026-08-04 ESPN's site.api began rejecting both browser-style and bare custom User-Agent strings, which returned 403 Forbidden for every request this plugin made. Requests now send an identifying agent with the project URL, which ESPN accepts. No behaviour change beyond the header.

Housekeeping, no behaviour change: scroll_display.py carried a second, unreferenced copy of the bundled fallback classes at module level -- the file was the pre-adoption and adopted versions concatenated rather than one replacing the other. The live fallback in scroll_display_legacy.py is untouched. Removing the dead copy is what makes a missing constant visible instead of appearing defined; that dead block is where the ones that broke scroll mode were hiding.

Fix scroll mode failing to start on LEDMatrix 3.2.0. The NCAA separator-icon paths stayed behind on the bundled fallback class when scroll display adopted the core orchestration, so building the scroll display raised AttributeError and scroll mode did not run at all on a 3.2.0 core. Switch mode and the fallback path were unaffected.

Scroll display now uses the core's shared sports-scroll orchestration (LEDMatrix 3.2.0) when available, falling back to the bundled implementation on older cores. No behaviour change: all harness renders are byte-for-byte identical.

Fix event start times rendering in UTC. The plugin looked for the LEDMatrix global timezone only on cache_manager.config_manager; on cores that expose config_manager via the plugin manager instead, that lookup found nothing and every start time was drawn in UTC even though the clock plugin was correct on the same device. Timezone resolution now checks the plugin override, then both config managers, then the host system zone, before falling back to UTC. Adds a documented timezone setting under Advanced Settings -- previously the key was not in the config schema, so hand-editing it had no effect.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed. Also enables the NCAA Men's league block by default so a fresh install shows games immediately (matching the other scoreboards).

Add display_durations.non_favorite_live per league: give live games without a favorite team a shorter on-screen turn than your favorites. Applies only when favorite teams are set and favorite_teams_only is off; defaults to 0 (off) for unchanged behavior.

Add exclude_teams (hide specific teams from the live rotation and recent/final scores — spoiler protection, takes precedence over favorite_teams/show_all_live) and favorite_live_boost (tune how many more turns your favorite's live game gets in the rotation vs other live games, 1 = even rotation, default 2).
